title: Circles
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Official outcomes a to c are tested; d (use IT) and e (promote use) are not questions. π is taken as 22/7 (or 3.14 when the question says so), as in the families. Grade 7 already found the circumference; Grade 8 adds the arc as a fraction θ/360 of it and the perimeter of a sector (the arc and two radii). The families tag these with the HOREB skill G9_ARC_LENGTH, which is kept so the practice engine still finds them. Working back from a perimeter to the radius (one family) goes a little beyond the outcome: teacher to confirm.

skills.key_step: The child says whether the given length is a radius or a diameter and writes the formula that fits before putting in numbers.

floor.prerequisite: Knows diameter is twice the radius.
floor.question: Radius 7 cm: diameter?

representations: a circle with radius and diameter marked
steps: Is it a radius or a diameter?

board.do: Draw a circle and mark a radius of 14 cm.

board.say: How long is the line right across?

misconceptions.ask: Is 14 the radius or the diameter?
Do we want the space inside or the distance round?
Does π add or multiply?
Is round longer or shorter than across?
C = 2πr: where is the 2?

checks.question: Circumference of a circle of radius 21 cm (π = 22/7)?
Circumference of a tin of diameter 7 cm?

skills.key_step: The child says one turn of a wheel (or one lap) is one circumference, then multiplies or divides by the number of turns.
representations: a wheel rolled along a line
steps: Multiply by the turns, or divide the distance by one lap.
contexts: a boda boda wheel on the road to Kitengela

board.do: Draw a wheel on a road and mark where a spot on the rim touches the road.
Point at the mark after one turn.
board.say: How far has the wheel moved?

board.do: Wait for the child to say one circumference.
The child marks two and three turns.

misconceptions.ask: Metres or centimetres?
How many turns?
Do laps add one at a time or repeat?
How many 220s fit in 1,100?
Is 70 cm across the whole wheel?

checks.question: A wheel of diameter 56 cm turns 50 times. Distance in metres?
A track of radius 35 m. Laps to run 2,200 m?

skills.key_step: The child writes the fraction θ/360 and checks it is less than one before multiplying by the circumference.

floor.prerequisite: Finds a fraction of a number.
floor.question: 60/360 of 132

representations: a paper circle folded into sectors
the angle as a fraction of 360
steps: Check: shorter than the whole circle.
contexts: a hedge along a curved shamba edge
a metal rim for a gate
the crust of a cake slice

board.do: Draw a circle of radius 21 cm with a 60° sector shaded.

board.say: What fraction of the whole turn is this?

misconceptions.ask: Is the arc the whole way round?
Is the full circle πr or 2πr?
Is an arc a length or an area?
Can an arc be longer than the circle?
Degrees or centimetres?
Is 60 degrees the same as 90?

checks.question: Arc of 45° on a circle of radius 28 cm?
Arc of 120° on a circle of radius 21 cm?

skills.key_step: The child turns the story into an angle at the centre (6 degrees a minute for a minute hand) before finding the arc.

floor.prerequisite: Knows a minute hand turns once an hour.
floor.question: Degrees in a full turn of the minute hand

steps: Find the angle from the story.

board.do: Draw a clock face with the minute hand at 12 and at 4.

board.say: How many minutes, and how many degrees?

misconceptions.ask: Did the hand go all the way round?
How many degrees in one minute?
How long for a full turn of the minute hand?
Which hand turns 30 degrees an hour?

checks.question: A minute hand of 14 cm. How far does its tip move in 15 minutes?
How many degrees does a minute hand turn in 25 minutes?

skills.key_step: The child traces the edge of the sector with a finger, naming the arc and both radii, before adding.
steps: Add a radius for each straight edge.
For a half circle, the straight edge is the diameter.
contexts: a slice of a round cake

board.do: Draw a sector of radius 7 m and angle 90°.
The child traces all the way round the edge.

misconceptions.ask: Does the fence go along the straight edges too?
How many straight edges?
Is the curved edge the whole circle?
Is the straight edge part of the perimeter?

checks.question: A sector of radius 14 m and angle 45°. Perimeter?
A half circle of radius 7 m. Perimeter?

skills.key_step: The child writes the perimeter as r terms (πr + 2r) and collects them into one before dividing.

floor.prerequisite: Solves an equation with a fraction coefficient.
floor.question: (36/7)r = 72

representations: the perimeter in terms of r
steps: Write the curved edge in r.
Write the straight edge in r.

board.do: Draw a half circle with the radius marked r.

board.say: How long is it in terms of r?

misconceptions.ask: Is the straight edge in the perimeter?
How many radii make the straight edge?
Is the curved edge the full circle?
How many r altogether?

checks.question: A half circle has a perimeter of 36 m. Radius (π = 22/7)?
A half circle has a perimeter of 108 m. Radius?
